Charu

Vijay, you asked on this podcast how I think about pleasure. I'm Manjula, I'm twenty-six, and I have a mango rule.
In summer, I eat one Alphonso mango every evening. Standing at the sink, juice running down my arms, no phone, no TV. Ten whole minutes. It's the best part of my day.
I don't eat five. I tried that once. By the fourth, I couldn't taste anything.
That's how I try to do everything. Real lunch breaks. A nap on Sundays. Dancing at weddings until my feet hurt. I think joy is serious business.
But I don't chase the next thrill. I don't need a bigger party every weekend. I need to actually be at the one I'm at.
And I still go to work, pay my bills and see my doctor when I should. The mango doesn't replace those. It just makes them bearable.
